pr_title: HTTP2: flush preface / settings frames when channel become active
pr_body:
Motivation:

We need to manually flush the channl when it becomes active and we wrote the preface / settigns frame as otherwise the remote peer might never see it.

Modifications:

- Flush after writing preface / settings
- Adjust unit test to verify the new behaviour
- Adjust unit tests to complete mocking everything before the connection is actually established

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/12089

issue_context.title: Client Http2ConnectionHandler: preface is not flushed on http2 start with prior-knowledge
issue_context.body:
### Expected behavior

Preface is flushed by client `Http2ConnectionHandler` on http2 start with prior-knowledge (aka plaintext) so connection is established (SETTINGS of both sides are sent) in timely manner - which corresponds to netty's http2 `tls/alpn` start.

### Actual behavior

Preface may be [not flushed](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/51eda20432568ffdf736a673abc6b5a44839413f/codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2ConnectionHandler.java#L358) on http2 start with prior-knowledge, so http2 connection is not established unless "next" handler knows this peculiarity and does initial redundant flush (e.g. in `channelActive()`).

### Steps to reproduce

Currently [test](https://github.com/jauntsdn/netty-websocket-http2/commit/97d037ac8209750a724b8e38483c388760cd2620) in netty based project, passes with [workaround](https://github.com/jauntsdn/netty-websocket-http2/commit/668bf0ef26a2f0d2cf7d28b913f708c72c2a0aca).

### Minimal yet complete reproducer code (or URL to code)

### Netty version

4.1.74.Final

review_comments: Consider having at least 1 test to make sure the new flag set to `false` works as expected.
please, don't forget about the test

```suggestion
            if (flushPreface && ctx.pipeline().get(SslHandler.class) == null) {
```
This avoids redundant flush with TLS connections, in other case `Config.flushPreface(false)` is needed for this much more common case. While `ctx.pipeline().get(SslHandler.class)` construct is uncommon for core netty http codecs, It is still used internally (Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec, WebSocketServerProtocolHandshakeHandler).

Otherwise I would suggest to change `Config.flushPreface` default to false.
Actually I think we should just let it flush always... The `SslHandler` will only propagate the flush if there was really something produced.
+1, flush is expensive only when there are pending data. otherwise, it becomes noop
